description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Resilience and Inclusive Trade Portfolio works from the conviction that trade facilitation only delivers on its poverty-reduction potential when it explicitly addresses the barriers faced by those most at risk of being left behind i.e. women, youth, persons with disabilities, and small-scale cross-border traders. The Portfolio operates across four interconnected areas: making regional food trade in staple crops more efficient, competitive, and climate-adaptive through improved standards compliance, storage and aggregation infrastructure, and access to finance; accelerating the movement of food aid-related cargo through green channels at One Stop Border Posts to reduce humanitarian supply chain bottlenecks; promoting trade reforms that remove specific barriers for small businesses — including Simplified Trade Regimes, Joint Border Committees, and streamlined border processes — while equipping traders with information, business development support, and formalisation pathways; and directly supporting women and youth to organise into cooperatives and access markets

recipient-country.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) accelerates economic integration across 20 sub-Saharan nations by designing regional programmes that reduce trade barriers, lower transit costs, and digitize border infrastructure. Spanning East, West, Central, Southern Africa, and the Horn, these initiatives modernise critical maritime ports and key trade corridors by replacing paper-heavy customs processes with automated digital single-window systems. By targeting green trade corridor development, supporting women and small businesses in cross-border trade, and mobilizing private capital through its commercial arm, Trade Catalyst Africa, TMA directly facilitates trade flow alignment with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) frameworks.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Number of resource centres serving traders with information and other trade support services

comment.narrative: 14 Resource centres serving more than 4,300 traders with information and other trade support services.
